neighbours.label: the predicate of a general statement about a class of mathematical or physical objects ('Z-modules are the same as...', 'vector functions can be...'): copula, modal or determiner right after a math-object subject
fire: In topology, compact metric spaces are always complete and totally bounded.
Every finite abelian group can be decomposed into a direct sum of cyclic groups.
Recall that orthogonal matrices are exactly the matrices whose inverse is their transpose.
As a rule, harmonic functions are smooth inside any open domain where they are defined.
In physics, conservative forces can be written as the gradient of a potential.
We note that normal subgroups are precisely the kernels of group homomorphisms.
By definition, eigenvectors of a matrix are nonzero vectors that it only rescales.
Over the reals, polynomials of odd degree always have at least one real root.
quiet: In winter, mountain cabins are always cold and hard to reach by road.
Every small village bakery can be found by the smell of bread in the morning.
Recall that old cathedrals are exactly the buildings tourists queue to photograph.
As a rule, house cats are lazy inside any warm room where they are allowed.
In cooking, soft cheeses can be stored in the fridge for about a week.
We note that local libraries are precisely the places students go to revise.
By tradition, wedding guests in the region are expected to bring sweet bread.
Over the summer, garden tomatoes always ripen faster on the sunny side.

notes: Card peaks on ' are', ' can', ' also', ' a' after math subjects; probes 0.4-0.7 for math statements, 0.02 for the same syntax about neighbours.
